wanted: For my decisions to feel like they actually bent the world - that following the stray and heaving the lid up before he could stop me produced consequences I had earned
For the 'measure/look-away' mechanic to feel like a real threat my choices could dodge, not a script the story was running me through
feared: That the fragment's inner voice ('Ask him what he threw in', 'Look at him', 'Look away') and the recurring flinch motif would make me feel puppeted - the story deciding my character's impulses and only letting me choose which pre-written outcome to read
That my agency was an illusion layered over a single linear plot
attention_intensified: 031: the lid slid and there was no water but a night sky inside, and the falling kit opened its orange eyes and said 'You took your time.' - the reveal that the stray did not find a fragment but escaped from one, and that the kit was what the Voyd learned to wear, all landed in one image - the single most gripping beat of the whole walk
attention_weakened: 030: the opening stretch of alley-following and back-and-forth dialogue ('You wrapped it?' / 'No.' / 'Good.' / 'P'taxx likes things that can be shelved.') - the setup was competent but slow and the real pressure (the knocks from the cistern) didn't arrive until the scene's final third
confused: 031: 'The Voyd. The name is not new. It is the door in the room behind the shop, seen from inside - the same ledger of looking-aways, the same filed fragment, the same countdown' arrived out of nowhere - on the Stray route I have never been inside the room behind the shop, never met the high door or the filed fragment, and the Antiquarian route is a different path I did not take; the story references shared canon/lore I have not been given, breaking the first-time-player illusion
residue: A clean, escalating dread: a thing that records your involuntary flinches and files them as evidence, a stranger who escaped one of these and carried his name under his skin, and a jammed cistern lid that can no longer close
The ending sits as a held breath - the kit named me, the lid is stuck open, and the frontier says the next move must confront the kit without letting the fragment choose my response first
I was left genuinely wanting to know what happens next - the right feeling for a mid-story stop
